nodes.label: Test definition schema as the SDK wire contract
nodes.author: Perfscale Team
nodes.rationale: The YAML/JSON test definition and summary export are chosen as the SDK's true cross-language wire contract rather than any Rust type: schemas, a validator (perfscale lint), an idempotent execution endpoint, and SummaryExport already exist. Additive-only versioning with a schemaVersion rejection gate is required because lenient parsing can silently produce wrong load tests (e.g. ignored multipart field sends an empty-body POST that looks green).

nodes.label: perfscale facade crate with curated re-exports
nodes.author: Perfscale Team
nodes.rationale: Chosen over stabilizing perfscale-core directly: the facade costs one more crate and re-export boilerplate but buys freedom to keep refactoring engine internals while downstreams (perfscaled, currently on git-main and broken twice in one week by signature changes) pin a semver surface. Engine global state (OnceLock clients/caches) and tokio runtime ownership must be scoped or documented before 1.0.

nodes.label: Thin language SDKs (builders + drivers, not engines)
nodes.author: Perfscale Team
nodes.rationale: JS/Python SDKs build schema-valid definitions and drive execution via CLI subprocess or agent HTTP instead of FFI/napi/pyo3 bindings: load generation is not latency-sensitive on the control path, so a subprocess launch is noise against a 30s test, while bindings would multiply the build matrix by platforms x runtime versions. Data types are generated from the JSON Schema; builder sugar is handwritten on top.
